# Visual and data credits

::: {.doc-lead}
The showcase uses real Flux compositions: authored scientific figures, public datasets and calculated examples. This page identifies their sources and what the views represent. It also credits the [colormaps, fonts and software](#software) that Flux and fluxplot are built on.
:::

## The figures and screenshots {#figures}

The materials and neuroscience figures were composed by Kort Driessen in a demonstration project. Their plot content, layout, labels and views are preserved. Captions and the demonstration manuscript were written for this site. Screenshots show development builds after the v0.3.0 release, using isolated copies of the selected work; the Slides workspace screenshot shows the Japan earthquakes example from Plots in Motion.

The close-ups and short clips in the guides (the Plots rail, Align & Arrange, plot reflow, sticky connectors, the X-ray, the Cursor settings, the Paper figures pane and the spelling checker) were captured in isolated demonstration projects. The tutorial plot placed in them, the dissections folder with its summary table and note, and the typed sentences are illustrative. The meanmark and fluxbox drawings in the plotting guides were made with fluxplot from synthetic values and say so beside each one.

The Library screenshot shows a demonstration bibliography for structural biology. Reader shows John Jumper and colleagues, “Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold,” Nature 596 (2021), licensed CC BY 4.0. The highlight and reading note were added for the demonstration. [Paper](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-021-03819-2) · [Licence](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

The image-stack guide shows illustrative cells generated for the website. The stack has two simulated fluorescence channels with time and depth, and a labelled layer for the cell outlines.

Timeline alignment diagrams use Flux's alignment operations to calculate the bar positions on a small geometric example. Close-ups show the real X-ray, property menu and Animator; the easing editor and animation-style screenshots use the same teaching deck.

## Slides {#slides}

The homepage plays examples from the Plots in Motion deck and the Flux film. The guides use examples from the film. All were authored in Flux and play through its native slide player. Each player names its source below the slide. The endpoints show the measured or computed values described below. Motion between endpoints interpolates the displayed values.

| Slide | Source and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Japan’s earthquakes, from the side | [USGS earthquake catalog](https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/search/) events of magnitude 5 and above, 1975–2025, over ETOPO1 shaded relief. The slide isolates a band across northern Honshu and plots distance along the section against depth at equal scale. |
| The Moon’s month | Computed illustration of lunar illumination and the phases visible from Earth over a synodic month. |
| A neuron, untangled | Layer 5 pyramidal neuron from mouse visual cortex, [Allen Cell Types Database specimen 480114344](https://celltypes.brain-map.org/experiment/morphology/480114344), reconstruction 491771446. The neuron is projected onto the slice plane, and the unfolded tree uses three-dimensional path lengths. |
| A sunflower’s golden angle | Computed seed layouts comparing patterns made by different angles between successive seeds, including approximately 137.5°. |
| Any figure can become a slide | The Flux mark, plotted, and shapes drawn in Flux. |
| Shapes that change shape | Computed geometry: a superquadric (sphere, cube and star states) and the catenoid–helicoid family of minimal surfaces. |
| Central limit theorem | Simulated samples from a Gamma(2, 0.5) population. |
| Spikes to rate | Simulated spike trains from an inhomogeneous Poisson process; no recording is implied. |
| Spatial transcriptomics | Simulated expression on a Visium-style hexagonal spot grid, embedded with PCA and UMAP. |
| Phyllotaxis | Vogel’s model: radius = c√n, angle = n × 137.5°, for 233 seeds. Spiral counts depend on scale. |
| Shadows contain a shape | Exact parallel-beam projections of three uniform disks at twelve angles. The final image is an unfiltered backprojection, so its blur is expected. |

The 3D slide uses WebGL. Browsers without it show Flux’s saved views of each step.

### In the film {#film}

The film on the homepage shows the two figures described under [Neuroscience](#neuroscience) and [Materials](#materials), and these examples.

| Slide | Source and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Visual response latency across brain regions | Region outlines from a coronal section of the [Allen Mouse Common Coordinate Framework, CCF2017](https://download.alleninstitute.org/informatics-archive/current-release/mouse_ccf/). **The latency values are synthetic and illustrative**, not recordings. |
| The fold becomes a fingerprint | C-alpha coordinates of crambin, [PDB 1CRN](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/1CRN). A contact is a C-alpha distance below 8 Å with sequence separation above 2. The motion is a change of representation, not protein unfolding. |
| From genes to programs | Airway RNA-seq, [GEO GSE52778](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE52778) (Himes et al. 2014, [doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0099625](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0099625)), read counts from the Bioconductor `airway` package. The 36 most variable genes are clustered into three descriptive groups, not validated pathways. |
| Agreement, revealed | First and second systolic blood-pressure readings from [NHANES 2017–2018](https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/2017/DataFiles/BPX_J.htm): a deterministic sample of 240 complete pairs. Descriptive and unweighted; not a population estimate. |
| Scatter plots sent to the agent | The Datasaurus Dozen: J. Matejka and G. Fitzmaurice (2017), [Same stats, different graphs](https://doi.org/10.1145/3025453.3025912), after Alberto Cairo's Datasaurus. |

The paper read and highlighted in the film is R. E. Kass, B. S. Caffo, M. Davidian, X.-L. Meng, B. Yu and N. Reid (2016), [Ten simple rules for effective statistical practice](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pcbi.1004961), *PLOS Computational Biology* 12, e1004961, shown under its [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) licence. The manuscript and the reply to reviewers in the film were written for the demonstration.

## The visual tour {#visual-tour}

Every clip in the [visual tour](/visual-tour/) was filmed in Flux on a copy of a demonstration project. Each clip's caption names its source, and the note at the end of the tour lists them all. The sources are collected here with their licences.

| Material | Source and licence |
|---|---|
| Phase portraits, bifurcation diagram, Lyapunov map, time trace and spectrum | Computed from a driven Duffing oscillator. |
| Protein figure | Panels a and b: the [AlphaFold Protein Structure Database](https://alphafold.ebi.ac.uk/) model of human p53 (CC BY 4.0) and the cryo-EM structures of the SARS-CoV-2 spike, [PDB 6VSB](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/6VSB) (Wrapp et al., *Science*, 2020) and [PDB 6VXX](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/6VXX) (Walls et al., *Cell*, 2020). The other panels, including the uptake curves, enzyme kinetics and simulation traces, are simulated. |
| Tuning figure and its dissections | Allen Brain Observatory, Visual Coding 2-photon, experiment 501940850 (Allen Institute for Brain Science), under the [Allen Institute terms](https://alleninstitute.org/legal/terms-of-use). |
| Heart model | [Z-Anatomy](https://www.z-anatomy.com/), CC BY-SA 4.0. The pressure, volume and ECG traces come from physiological models. |
| Black holes and merger | Computed from the Kerr metric, with a synthetic post-Newtonian waveform. |
| The Sun | NASA/SDO and the AIA, EVE and HMI science teams. Public domain. |
| Arabidopsis shoot meristem | Galvan-Ampudia, Cerutti et al. (2020), *eLife*; [Zenodo 3737795](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.3737795). CC BY 4.0. |
| Night side of the Earth | Earth Science and Remote Sensing Unit, NASA Johnson Space Center, frames ISS030-E-68921 to 69120. Public domain. |
| Image thumbnails in the Plots rail | Sakaguchi, Leiwe and Imai (2018), *eLife*, CC BY; FISBe (Mais, Hirsch et al., 2024), from Janelia FlyLight, CC BY 4.0; Clark, Battistara and Benton (2022), *eLife*, CC0; the [Human Protein Atlas](https://www.proteinatlas.org/), CC BY 4.0; Winfree, El-Achkar and Ferkowicz (2022), CC BY 4.0. |
| Sea ice, river discharge and the map of South America | Sea ice: [NSIDC Sea Ice Index, Version 4](https://nsidc.org/data/g02135) (Fetterer, Knowles, Meier, Savoie and Windnagel). Rivers and borders: [Natural Earth](https://www.naturalearthdata.com/), public domain. Relief: NOAA ETOPO1 (Amante and Eakins, 2009). The discharge curves are synthetic. |
| White light is every colour | A ray-traced prism. The spectrum is the SAO2010 solar reference spectrum: K. Chance and R. L. Kurucz (2010), [doi:10.1016/j.jqsrt.2010.01.036](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jqsrt.2010.01.036). |
| A neuron and its synapses | A layer 2/3 pyramidal cell of mouse visual cortex from the [MICrONS](https://www.microns-explorer.org/) cubic millimetre, with its input synapses (MICrONS Consortium, 2025). CC BY 4.0. |
| Japan's earthquakes | [USGS earthquake catalog](https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/search/), magnitude 5 and above, 1975–2025, over ETOPO1 relief. |
| Hurricane tracks | IBTrACS version 4: Knapp et al. (2010), [doi:10.1175/2009BAMS2755.1](https://doi.org/10.1175/2009BAMS2755.1), NOAA NCEI. Coastlines: Natural Earth. |
| The rhythm of the elements | First ionization energies from the [PubChem periodic table](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/periodic-table/). |
| Sunflower | Computed. |
| Gravitational-wave strain | LIGO Hanford and Livingston strain for GW150914 from the [Gravitational Wave Open Science Center](https://gwosc.org/) (LIGO Scientific Collaboration and Virgo Collaboration). CC BY 4.0. |
| Mouse-brain cells and their UMAP | MERFISH measurements from the Zhuang laboratory (Zhang et al., *Nature*, 2023) from the Allen Brain Cell Atlas (Allen Institute for Brain Science), dataset [Zhuang-ABCA-4](https://alleninstitute.github.io/abc_atlas_access/descriptions/Zhuang-ABCA-4.html). CC BY 4.0. The UMAP was computed for the clip. |
| Brain, electrodes and EEG traces | Cortex: the FreeSurfer fsaverage surface (Fischl, 2012) with Desikan–Killiany regions, read with MNE-Python (Gramfort et al., 2013). Electrodes: the standard 10–20 montage. The traces are synthetic. |
| Penguin measurements | Palmer Station Antarctica LTER: Gorman, Williams and Fraser (2014), [doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0090081](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0090081). CC0. |

Grant on Daphne Major: Grant and Grant (2014), [Dryad](https://doi.org/10.5061/dryad.vc348), CC0; beak depths of 1976 and 1978 as published in Ramsey and Schafer, *The Statistical Sleuth*; museum specimen measurements from David Lack, archived on Dryad, CC0. Engraving: John Gould, in Darwin's *Journal of Researches* (1845), public domain. |
| Papers open in Reader | Jumper et al. (2021), [Highly accurate protein structure prediction with AlphaFold](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-021-03819-2), and Tunyasuvunakool et al. (2021), [Highly accurate protein structure prediction for the human proteome](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-021-03828-1), *Nature* 596. Both CC BY 4.0. |

The manuscript “Reading a protein across scales” and its authors were invented for the tour; its references are real. Journal names in the export examples identify the submission formats Flux prepares. Flux is not affiliated with or endorsed by those journals.

## Neuroscience {#neuroscience}

**Data and anatomical models: Allen Institute for Brain Science.** The response plots use [Allen Brain Observatory Visual Coding](https://brain-map.org/our-research/circuits-behavior/visual-coding) experiment **501940850**, container **511510688**: 143 cells in mouse lateral visual cortex (VISl), with eight drift directions and five temporal frequencies. The source [analysis file](https://api.brain-map.org/api/v2/well_known_file_download/515078316) provides the response arrays used by the demonstration analyses.

The brain geometry and coronal view use the [Allen Mouse Common Coordinate Framework, CCF2017](https://download.alleninstitute.org/informatics-archive/current-release/mouse_ccf/). Neuronal silhouettes and the small mesh reconstruction use [MICrONS](https://www.microns-explorer.org/) reconstructions. These anatomical examples are separate from the functionally recorded cells.

The circular network connects similar response profiles; it is not a map of anatomical synapses.

Relevant publications:

- de Vries et al. (2020), [A large-scale standardized physiological survey reveals functional organization of the mouse visual cortex](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41593-019-0550-9).
- Wang et al. (2020), [The Allen Mouse Brain Common Coordinate Framework: A 3D Reference Atlas](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2020.04.007).
- MICrONS Consortium (2025), [Functional connectomics spanning multiple areas of mouse visual cortex](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-08790-w).

Allen resources retain the [Allen Institute terms](https://alleninstitute.org/legal/terms-of-use) and [citation policy](https://alleninstitute.org/legal/citation-policy). MICrONS resources retain the terms linked by the source project. The website's software license does not relicense these datasets. No endorsement by the data providers is implied.

## Materials and electronic structure {#materials}

The materials plate combines several kinds of information:

| View | Source and interpretation |
|---|---|
| Stiffness–density chart | Typical material values entered by hand, with hand-fitted family envelopes; a reference illustration. |
| Bracket stress field | A finite-element calculation using Gmsh and scikit-fem. |
| Stress around a circular hole | The analytic Kirsch solution, with stress concentration factor 3. |
| MgB₂ Fermi surface and sections | The `mgb2_vfz.frmsf` example from [FermiSurfer](https://github.com/mitsuaki1987/fermisurfer/tree/master/examples). |
| Density of states | An illustrative model calculation. |
| Crystal structures | Public crystallographic records listed below. |

Crystal models use the [Crystallography Open Database](https://www.crystallography.net/cod/): [CaTiO₃, 1000022](https://www.crystallography.net/cod/1000022.html), [YBa₂Cu₃O₇, 1001452](https://www.crystallography.net/cod/1001452.html), [NaCl, 9000629](https://www.crystallography.net/cod/9000629.html), and [silicon, 9011998](https://www.crystallography.net/cod/9011998.html). Their original publication citations are included in the linked records; COD data are available under CC0.

FermiSurfer: M. Kawamura (2019), [Fermi-surface viewer providing multiple representation schemes](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cpc.2019.01.017). The demonstration renders derived geometry and sections from the example input; it does not redistribute the original input dataset as a download.

## Scientific images {#scientific-images}

The cyan and magenta stack in the [image guide](/docs/fluximg.html) is a synthetic fluorescence example. Its channels, depth and time samples, segmented cell outlines and attached object values were generated for the demonstration. They illustrate how to inspect an image and do not represent measurements from a specimen.

## Software, fonts and colours {#software}

Flux supplies the phyllotaxis mark, the application and the native slide player. Everything else on this list is other people's work that Flux, fluxplot or this website uses. The complete lists, with every bundled library and its licence, are the notices in the [Flux](https://github.com/fluxsci/flux/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and [fluxplot](https://github.com/fluxsci/fluxplot/blob/main/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) repositories.

| matplotlib | The Matplotlib Development Team | Hunter (2007), *Computing in Science & Engineering* 9, 90–95, [doi:10.1109/MCSE.2007.55](https://doi.org/10.1109/MCSE.2007.55) | Matplotlib licence |
| Crameri | Fabio Crameri | Crameri (2018), Scientific colour maps, Zenodo, [doi:10.5281/zenodo.1243862](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.1243862); Crameri, Shephard and Heron (2020), *Nature Communications* 11, 5444, [doi:10.1038/s41467-020-19160-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-19160-7) | MIT |

Flux's "green" ramp in the Flexoki palette is the author's own, built around Paul Tol's bright green as its main shade; Flexoki's green is kept under the name "olive". The five house maps in the `flexoki` collection were made for fluxplot.

Some maps in the matplotlib collection have authors of their own:

- viridis, magma, inferno and plasma: Nathaniel J. Smith, Stéfan van der Walt and Eric Firing (CC0).
- cividis: Nuñez, Anderton and Renslow (2018), *PLOS ONE* 13, e0199239, [doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0199239](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0199239).
- turbo: Anton Mikhailov, Google (Apache-2.0).
- twilight: Bastian Bechtold.
- coolwarm: Kenneth Moreland (2009), [doi:10.1007/978-3-642-10520-3_9](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-642-10520-3_9).
- cubehelix: D. A. Green (2011), *Bulletin of the Astronomical Society of India* 39, 289–295.
- The Brewer maps: ColorBrewer, as above. The `gist` maps: Yorick, The Regents of the University of California. Wistia: Wistia (MIT). The `tab` palettes: Vega, after Tableau. berlin, managua and vanimo: Fabio Crameri.

The colour-vision simulation in **View as** and in fluxplot's colour checks uses the model of Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes (2009), *IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics* 15, 1291–1298, [doi:10.1109/TVCG.2009.113](https://doi.org/10.1109/TVCG.2009.113).

### Fonts and icons {#fonts}

Flux and this website use Gelasio (The Gelasio Project Authors, [SIL Open Font License 1.1](/assets/fonts/OFL.txt)) beside the system's Georgia. Mathematics in Flux is set with KaTeX and its fonts (Khan Academy and contributors, MIT). Most of Flux's interface icons come from [Lucide](https://lucide.dev) (ISC).

The journal export presets follow the public author guidelines of Nature, Science, Cell and bioRxiv. Flux is not affiliated with or endorsed by those journals.

### fluxplot {#software-in-fluxplot}

fluxplot builds on [Matplotlib](https://matplotlib.org), NumPy, SciPy, seaborn, lxml and CMasher. Its statistics follow the published methods named in the [statistics guide](/docs/statistics.html), and its 3D viewer uses three.js.

### This website {#software-in-website}

The site is built with [Quarto](https://quarto.org). The slide players use Flux's own runtime with Svelte, three.js, css-tree and kiwi; their licence notices are published with the site: [three.js](/assets/licenses/three-LICENSE.txt), [Svelte](/assets/licenses/svelte-LICENSE.txt), [css-tree](/assets/licenses/css-tree-LICENSE.txt) and [kiwi](/assets/licenses/lume-kiwi-LICENSE.txt).

### Inspiration {#inspiration}

Two apps shaped how Flux works: [Figma](https://www.figma.com/) was the main inspiration for Figure, and [Obsidian](https://obsidian.md/) for Paper. Flux contains no code from either and is not affiliated with them.
